findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_screeners" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Return metadata for all 24 stock screeners on the platform: slug, name, description, category, tier, whether the caller can read it, and its row fields with the…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_market_momentum · Private data: get_chart_patterns, search_patterns, get_options_flow_ranked, get_options_flow_sentiment, search_stocks, search_setups · Public sink: get_market_momentum.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_market_momentum · Private data: get_chart_patterns, search_patterns, get_options_flow_ranked, get_options_flow_sentiment, search_stocks, search_setups · Public sink: get_market_momentum

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_chart_patterns" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
